teach_overlay.label: 20,000 HUMAN GENES → >10,000,000,000 (10^10) UNIQUE ANTIBODIES VIA V(D)J DNA SPLICING (40 V × 23 D × 6 J + JUNCTIONS)
teach_overlay.detail: Inked human genome vs antibody diversity chart on period paper comparing ~20,000 total human protein-coding genes against >10,000,000,000 (10^10) unique B-cell antibody locks created by shuffling ~40 V, 23 D, and 6 J heavy-chain gene segments with light-chain V-J segments and random junctional nucleotides
teach_overlay.scale: if every one of your twenty thousand human genes were a single book, your immune system couldn't fill a small town library — yet by cutting and shuffling sentences from just a few dozen pages like a slot machine, your white blood cells print ten billion different security passcodes
